headline: 134 Years Ago, India's Voice Reached Parliament
meta_description: On July 26, 1892, Dadabhai Naoroji became the first Indian elected to British Parliament, challenging colonial exploitation with economic theory.
summary_short: 134 years ago, merchant and scholar Dadabhai Naoroji made history as the first Indian elected to British Parliament, armed with evidence of economic exploitation.
body:
On July 26, 1892, Dadabhai Naoroji was elected to the British Parliament, becoming the first Indian ever to hold the position. A merchant, scholar, and founding member of the Indian National Congress, Naoroji arrived in Westminster with a radical argument: that British rule was systematically draining India's wealth. He estimated between 200 and 300 million sterling left the Indian economy annually through exploitative laws and financial incentives that pushed capital toward Britain rather than keeping it at home. When taking office, Naoroji refused to swear on the Bible, instead using the Zoroastrian holy codex—a small act of conviction that Parliament granted him. Mahatma Gandhi would later say Indians looked up to Naoroji "as children look up to the father."

Naoroji's intellectual contribution proved as powerful as his presence. His book *Poverty and Un-British Rule in India* laid out the economic case for why colonialism impoverished nations, translating outrage into measurable argument. The "drain theory" seemed obvious in hindsight, but in the 1890s, articulating it in precise economic terms gave early Indian nationalists the language they needed. Beyond India's struggles, Naoroji held deep sympathy for Irish independence efforts unfolding simultaneously—his vision of justice crossed borders.

More than a century later, the British government recognized his legacy. In 2014, then Deputy Prime Minister Nick Clegg launched the Dadabhai Naoroji Awards to honor contributions to UK-India relations, ensuring that the man who once sat alone in Parliament became a bridge between nations rather than a footnote.
quick_facts: First Indian ever elected to British Parliament, July 26, 1892
Estimated 200-300 million sterling drained from India annually
Used Zoroastrian holy codex instead of Bible for oath of office
Authored *Poverty and Un-British Rule in India*, influencing nationalists
